boards.title: Your First Weekend at New York University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A first-weekend walking sequence through NYU’s Washington Square campus, mixing orientation stops, study spaces, arts, and public outdoor landmarks.

cards.title: Start at Washington Square Park
cards.subtitle: Campus center in Greenwich Village
cards.notes: Begin beneath the arch, orient yourself to the surrounding NYU buildings, then take a slow loop through the public park before choosing your next stop.
cards.short_summary: Use NYU’s unofficial quad as the starting point for learning the campus geography.
cards.evidence_claim: NYU identifies Washington Square Park as the heart and center of its campus, with university buildings around its perimeter.
cards.access_notes: Public city park; follow posted NYC Parks rules.

cards.title: Meet under the Washington Square Arch
cards.subtitle: Washington Square Park
cards.notes: Pick the arch as an easy landmark for meeting a classmate, then use the view through it to place Fifth Avenue and the north side of the park.
cards.short_summary: A clearly identifiable landmark for a first campus meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: NYU describes the Washington Square Arch as one of the park’s most recognizable areas and notes that visitors commonly take photos there.
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors in Washington Square Park.

cards.title: Find the Kimmel Center
cards.subtitle: 60 Washington Square South
cards.notes: Stop in to locate student-life services and make a note of the building for future club meetings, ticketing, campus programs, and dining options.
cards.short_summary: A practical orientation stop for student organizations and campus services.
cards.evidence_claim: NYU says the Kimmel Center houses most student clubs, communities, and organizations, along with student-life offices and two dining options.
cards.access_notes: NYU building access may require a current NYU ID.

cards.title: Get acquainted with Bobst
cards.subtitle: 70 Washington Square South
cards.notes: Walk through the first-floor study and lounge area, find the service points, and save the library’s location page before your first research assignment.
cards.short_summary: Locate NYU’s flagship library and its first-floor study services.
cards.evidence_claim: NYU Libraries identifies Bobst as its 12-story flagship library and lists study spaces, borrowing, research help, and other services there.
cards.access_notes: Current NYU students, faculty, and staff may access library buildings; visitors need advance sponsorship.

cards.title: Ask a librarian one question
cards.subtitle: First floor, Bobst Library
cards.notes: Bring a course topic or a question about finding materials and introduce yourself to the research-help desk while you are already learning the building.
cards.short_summary: Make research support feel familiar before coursework accelerates.
cards.evidence_claim: NYU Libraries states that in-person general reference help is available at the Reference Desk on Bobst Library’s first floor during business hours.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Bobst; confirm building hours and eligibility before visiting.

cards.title: See the Paulson Center commons
cards.subtitle: 181 Mercer Street
cards.notes: Walk through the Commons and note the building’s academic, recreation, rehearsal, and study functions so it is easier to recognize on your first busy week.
cards.short_summary: A single building that combines academic, recreation, and student spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: NYU describes the Paulson Center as containing student and faculty housing, study spaces, a Commons, performing-arts spaces, athletics and recreation, and classrooms.
cards.access_notes: NYU building access may require a current NYU ID.

cards.entity_name: Skirball Center for the Performing Arts
cards.title: Locate the Skirball Center
cards.subtitle: 566 LaGuardia Place
cards.notes: Find the entrance and check the calendar for a future performance, talk, or campus event that fits your interests and schedule.
cards.short_summary: Get oriented to one of Lower Manhattan’s major performance venues.
cards.evidence_claim: NYU identifies the Skirball Center for Performing Arts as one of the largest performance spaces in Lower Manhattan.
cards.access_notes: Event entry and ticket requirements vary by program; consult the venue’s current calendar.

cards.title: Step into the Grey Art Museum
cards.subtitle: 18 Cooper Square
cards.notes: Use the museum as a compact arts stop: look at the current exhibition, check gallery guidance at entry, and return when you have more time to browse.
cards.short_summary: Add a museum visit to the first-weekend campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: NYU’s Washington Square tour identifies the Grey Art Gallery as located in the Silver Center for Arts and Science.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current exhibitions, hours, and visitor policies with the museum before going.

cards.title: Pin the Academic Resource Center
cards.subtitle: 18 Washington Place
cards.notes: Save the ARC address and look around its shared spaces so you know where to return for tutoring, meetings, computing, or a quieter reset.
cards.short_summary: Identify a central campus building with tutoring and student-use spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: NYU says the Academic Resource Center at 18 Washington Place contains student lounges, tutoring and meeting spaces, classrooms, offices, and a computer lab.
cards.access_notes: NYU building access may require a current NYU ID.

cards.entity_name: Global Center for Academic and Spiritual Life
cards.title: End at the Global Center
cards.subtitle: 238 Thompson Street
cards.notes: Finish by locating the Global Center and checking its current programs, leaving yourself with one reliable campus destination for future reflection or community events.
cards.short_summary: A final orientation stop for a campus community and program space.
cards.evidence_claim: NYU’s Washington Square tour lists the Global Center for Academic and Spiritual Life as a campus destination on Thompson Street.
cards.access_notes: Check the center’s current program and building-access information before attending an event.
